title: (The Song of Moses — Hebrew poetry, grouped by poetic units)

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Listen, you heavens, and I will speak; hear, you earth, the words of my mouth. Let my teaching fall like rain and my words descend like dew, like showers on new grass, like abundant rain on tender plants." — Deut 32:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Song of Moses opens with a call for all creation to listen, and with a beautiful picture of how God's Word works: "Let my teaching fall like rain... like showers on new grass." Moses does not compare God's Word to a hammer or a storm here, but to gentle, life-giving rain and dew. God's truth comes to nourish, to soften, to bring growth — quietly soaking into the soil of our hearts.

There is deep encouragement in this image. Sometimes we may feel that God's Word is not doing much in us. We read, we listen, and we wonder if anything is really changing. But rain does its work slowly and often unseen. It soaks in gradually, and the growth comes in time. So it is with Scripture. Even when we cannot feel it, God's Word is watering our souls, softening hard ground, and bringing life to what looked barren.

This should shape how we come to the Bible — not merely to gather information, but to be nourished. We open Scripture the way dry ground receives rain, hungry for the life it brings.

Jesus is the ultimate living water, and His words are "full of the Spirit and life" (John 6:63). When we let His teaching fall on us like rain, we grow. So do not despise the days of slow, quiet growth. Keep letting the Word soak in. Like tender plants under gentle showers, your soul is being nourished by the God who sends His Word to give life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I come to God's Word hungry to be nourished, or only for information?
2. Am I patient with the slow, often unseen growth God's Word brings?
3. How can I let Scripture "soak in" more deeply this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let Your Word fall on my heart like gentle rain, softening, nourishing, and bringing growth. Even when I cannot feel it, water my soul with Your truth and give me life through it. Amen.
